audit.title: U.S. Government Macroeconomic Data Feeds

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: The implied question is "what are the feed addresses?" and the answer is a literal `Loading...` placeholder. Nothing self-contained to lift. Highest-severity gap.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Clean hierarchy — 1 H1, max depth H3, 0 level skips — but the core unit (an address table) doesn't exist in served content; only a "Networks → Ethereum Mainnet" shell.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: 0 numerals, 0 hex addresses, 0 units in prose. Catastrophic for an addresses page, which should be dense with contract addresses, decimals, and heartbeat intervals.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 11 links (10 internal, 1 external blog); sensible cross-links to best-practices and LINK-token pages, but 0 primary sources (e.g., U.S. Dept. of Commerce data origin).

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: No definition of what these feeds are or what data they carry; a reader learns nothing quotable about the product.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Valid dual JSON-LD, canonical, `inLanguage`, complete OG/Twitter. Undercut by `datePublished`==`dateModified` (never-revised signal), tokenized junk `keywords`, template `about` entries ("Content about government"), and a nonsensical `programmingLanguage: Go` on an addresses page.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No read-a-feed example; an agent has no runnable path from this page to actually consuming an address.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Targets a real intent ("US gov macro feed address") but doesn't answer it statically; no per-feed rows, no symptom/how-to phrasing.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: What little prose exists is clean and consistent. Strong on the fraction present.

audit.summary: This is a feed-address reference page whose entire reason for existing — the contract addresses, feed names, network details, and heartbeats — is rendered **client-side** ("More Details / Loading…") and therefore invisible to generative engines and crawlers that read the served HTML. The measured facts confirm the void: 93 words total, 0 numerals, 0 hex identifiers, 0 tables. Metadata scaffolding (valid `TechArticle` + `BreadcrumbList` JSON-LD, canonical, full OG/Twitter tags) is the page's one genuine strength, but schema quality can't rescue a page that ships no answer. The headline verdict: an engine asked "what is the Chainlink US Government Macroeconomic feed address on Ethereum?" gets nothing liftable from this page — the single highest-impact fix is server-rendering the address data into the static HTML.

recommendations.title: Server-render the feed address table
recommendations.issue: `Loading...` — the actual addresses are client-side only.
recommendations.change: Emit the address data as a static HTML `<table>` in the served page: columns for Feed name, Proxy address (`0x…`), Asset/data description, Deviation, Heartbeat, Decimals, per network. Even a `<noscript>` fallback table would make the data retrievable.
recommendations.why: Retrieval and citation are impossible when the answer isn't in the served HTML; this is the difference between the page being usable vs. invisible to every engine and agent.

recommendations.title: Add hex addresses and numeric specifics to prose/table
recommendations.change: Ensure each feed row shows the full `0x` proxy address, decimals, and update cadence; these quantitative specifics are the highest-lift content type for generative visibility.
recommendations.why: Quantitative, verbatim-liftable facts (addresses, decimals, heartbeats) are exactly what engines cite; qualitative shells underperform.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/question-phrased headings and a one-line canonical definition
recommendations.where: Top of page, under the H1.
recommendations.issue: Page opens with a link row, no definition of what these feeds provide.
recommendations.change: Add a 1–2 sentence liftable lead: "Chainlink U.S. Government Macroeconomic Data Feeds provide on-chain access to official U.S. Department of Commerce macroeconomic indicators (e.g., GDP). Contract addresses per network are listed below." Add an H3 phrased as the query, e.g. "What is the feed address on Ethereum Mainnet?"
recommendations.why: Devs/agents query by question and symptom; question-phrased headings win retrieval that concept shells lose, and a canonical definition gives engines something to quote.

recommendations.title: Fix auto-generated schema noise
recommendations.change: Remove the irrelevant `programmingLanguage`/`Programming Model` properties for a non-code page, replace token-salad `keywords` with real entities (e.g., "Chainlink Data Feeds, GDP, U.S. macroeconomic data"), and give `about` meaningful descriptions.
recommendations.why: Accurate structured metadata supports entity resolution and E-E-A-T; junk fields dilute trust signals.

recommendations.title: Surface a genuine last-updated signal
recommendations.change: Stamp `dateModified` from real content revisions and display a visible "Last updated" date near the address table.
recommendations.why: Visible freshness is an independent trust/ranking signal for feed reference data that changes over time.

recommendations.title: Add a minimal read-a-feed code example with imports
recommendations.issue: 0 code fences; no path from address to consumption.
recommendations.change: Add a short, complete Solidity or ethers.js `latestRoundData()` snippet using one of the listed proxy addresses, labeled by language and network.
recommendations.why: Complete, copy-pasteable snippets let coding agents complete the task directly from the page.

antiPatterns: **Wall-of-nothing / empty shell:** the primary content is a `Loading...` placeholder — the answer is absent from served HTML.
**Template/generator schema artifacts:** `programmingLanguage: Go`, tokenized `keywords`, boilerplate `about` descriptions on a data-reference page.
offPageNotes: **Client-side rendering is arguably a site-level framework decision**; the fix (static/SSR emission of feed tables) likely applies to every `/addresses` page across `docs.chain.link`, not just this one — worth escalating platform-wide.
Consider an `llms.txt` and ensuring these address pages are in the sitemap so engines discover the (once-rendered) data.
Raw `<head>` was provided and parsed cleanly; no metadata assumptions were needed.
